text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Liberal Free Democrats advocates more public debt. Coalition is undecided about it, while Finance Minister confirms plans to sell Deutsche Telekom shares to raise public money
- New building as part of German Library is opened in Frankfurt
- "Hidden poverty in east Germany" according to a new study
- The majority in the Bundestag lower of parliament are oppposed to the spelling
- Plans for Bonn to sell Telekom shares move the market. The company itself is surprised by Waigel's announcement
- DIW economic institute expects impulses from export
HANDELSBLATT

- Gold deposits of the Bundesbank are not safe from Bonn coalition. Wrestling over Chancellor Helmut Kohl's savings plans. Finance Minister confirms plans to sell Deutsche Telekom shares. Bonn coalition mobilises the last reserves to cover tax shortfall of until 20 billion marks
- There is risk that in 1998 pension contributions will to up
- New banking giant in Berlin. The Berlin Bank Gesellschaft and Nord/LB want to merge
- Lufthansa in global "star alliance" space project
- Transrapid is positively assessed by Transport Ministry
- Employers and workers councils at Daimler-Benz have agreed on their own "alliance for jobs"
- Saxony premier Kurt Biedenkopf stands by his criticism of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's renewed candidacy in next year's general election
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Finance Minister Theo Waigel considers selling state's Deutsche Telekom shares. New holes in the budget should be closed apart from cutting back on public spending and increasing debt
- New study indicates increase in poverty in eastern Germany in seven years since German unification
- Bank Gesellschaft Berlin bank merges with Nord/LB to create mammoth bank
- DIE WELT
- Raising taxes and selling shares? New tax revenue shortfalls present new worries for the coalition
- Finance Minister Theo Waigel under pressure as search for successful concept for cutting public spending seems to elude the ruling coalition
- Trial of ex-property magnate Juergen Schneider opens on June 30. Maximum sentence would be ten years

- "Star Alliance" the new giant in the world space industry. Lufthansa and cooperation partners agree to global alliance. Bonus miles will in future be mutually acknowledged. Improved service is also promised
- Waigel confuses Deutsche Telekom shareholders. Post ministry says the government can only sell its shares in the former state company outside the stock exchange
- Transport Minister Matthis Wissman defended his concept for Transrapid against criticism of opposition Social Democrats in parliament
